newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bank shares drop back on Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bank shares drop back on Costello.

text.p: Australian bank shares fell in late trade on Tuesday as profit-takers moved in on the first whiff of disappointment over the recent merger speculation.

Treasurer Peter Costello's afternoon comments that the Wallis Inquiry into the financial system would not report until after April 7 disappointed a market hoping that it would find out soon whether the inquiry would pave the way for more mergers. Westpac Banking Corp closed down three cents on the day at A$7.46, but down 15 cents from its A$7.61 high.
Westpac has rallied over five percent from A$7.04 in the past week.

Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, the other major bank seen most vulnerable to takeover, closed down 10.5 cents at A$8.17 and down 24.4 cents from its A$8.419 intraday high. ANZ has rallied over six percent from A$7.70 in the past week.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia closed down eight cents at A$12.70 and down 29 cents from its A$12.99 high.

"The market was a little bit lazy through the day and when Costello said the report wouldn't be released for a couple of weeks, people just decided it was time to take profits," said one Sydney broker.
Costello told parliament he would not be in a position to receive the report, brief the government and release the report until after April 7.
There had been widespread speculation in the press and in the markets that the report, which was due to be completed by March 31, would be released this week.
Bank shares rallied sharply on Monday as talk raced around the market that the report was imminent.
Leading businessman Stan Wallis chaired the official Financial System Inquiry, which began in June last year and is due to report to the government before the end of March.

The Wallis report is expected to recommend the scrapping of the "Six Pillars" policy set by the former Labor government, which prevents the four major banks from merging with each other or the two largest insurance and superannuation groups, AMP Group or National Mutual Holdings Ltd.
Wallis is also expected to make recommendations on prudential supervision, desposit insurance and foreign investment in banking.
Westpac and ANZ are seen the most likely takeover targets, while National Australia Bank Ltd is seen the strongest and most likely predator.
